DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)

The patient's presentation of burning pain, paresthesias, weakness, fasciculations, and absent reflexes is highly suggestive of a motor neuron disease. The specific combination of upper motor neuron signs (fasciculations, though reflexes are absent, suggesting mixed pathology or LMN predominance) and lower motor neuron signs points away from a simple cervical radiculopathy or diabetic neuropathy. I will proceed with a diagnosis of ALS based on the clinical evidence of mixed UMN and LMN findings, despite the pain component which can sometimes accompany ALS.
